edges.description: Occlusion creates a severely hypoperfused core and a potentially salvageable penumbra with residual perfusion.
Energy failure disrupts ionic gradients and glutamate handling, triggering calcium overload, oxidative injury, and cell death.
Ischemic injury activates vascular, glial, and immune responses in the neurovascular unit.
Energy failure activates macroautophagy within hours of occlusion, with autophagosome numbers and autophagy-marker levels in the ischemic penumbra rising over the following days.
Astrocytes and cerebral endothelial cells within the ischemic territory undergo acute cellular senescence following arterial occlusion.

edges.description: Microglial and vascular inflammatory signaling within the neurovascular unit provides the priming and danger signals for NLRP3 inflammasome assembly in the peri-infarct penumbra.

edges.description: Loss of cathepsin D-dependent lysosomal function aggravates, and its restoration protects against, oxygen-glucose deprivation-induced neuronal cell death, adding a lysosomal-clearance-failure route to excitotoxic and oxidative neuronal injury.

The senescence-associated secretory phenotype (MMP-3, IL-1alpha, IL-6) released by senescent astrocytes and endothelial cells adds to neurovascular inflammatory signaling and blood-brain barrier injury within the ischemic hemisphere.

nodes.description: Anticoagulation, particularly direct oral anticoagulant therapy when appropriate, is used after ischemic stroke associated with atrial fibrillation to reduce recurrent embolic events while managing hemorrhage risk.

evidence.reference_title: Antithrombotic treatment for secondary prevention of stroke and other thromboembolic events in patients with stroke or transient ischemic attack and non-valvular atrial fibrillation: A European Stroke Organisation guideline.
evidence.snippet: In patients with atrial fibrillation and previous stroke or transient ischemic attack, oral anticoagulants reduce the risk of recurrence over antiplatelets or no antithrombotic treatment.

nodes.description: Antiplatelet therapy reduces recurrent ischemic events after non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack, with duration and intensity balanced against bleeding risk.

evidence.reference_title: Benefits and Risks of Dual Versus Single Antiplatelet Therapy for Secondary Stroke Prevention: A Systematic Review for the 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack.
evidence.snippet: DAPT was more effective than SAPT for prevention of secondary ischemic stroke when initiated early after the onset of minor stroke/high-risk transient ischemic attack and treatment duration was <90 days.

nodes.description: Middle cerebral artery occlusion triggers acute cellular senescence in astrocytes and cerebral endothelial cells within the ischemic hemisphere, marked by p16INK4a upregulation and a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) of MMP-3, IL-1alpha, and IL-6. Senolytic clearance of these senescent cells, whether systemic (ABT-263) or local (targeted lenti-INK-ATTAC), reduces SASP factor levels and improves neurological and locomotor outcomes after occlusion. A senescence-associated blood gene-expression signature is independently associated with worse 90-day functional outcome in acute ischemic stroke patients.
nodes.id: Astrocyte and Cerebral Endothelial Cell Senescence

nodes.description: Macroautophagy is activated within the ischemic penumbra after arterial occlusion, with autophagosome numbers and autophagy-marker (Beclin-1, LC3B) levels rising early and then declining over the following days as autophagic flux weakens. In parallel, the lysosomal protease cathepsin D (CTSD) is progressively lost, and this lysosomal dysfunction, rather than autophagy induction itself, is the step this node conforms to: loss of CTSD is sufficient to cause lysosomal dysfunction and aggravates neuronal death under oxygen-glucose deprivation, while restoring CTSD activity protects neurons.

evidence.reference_title: Restoration of CTSD (cathepsin D) and lysosomal function in stroke is neuroprotective.
evidence.snippet: Our results show a time-dependent decrease in CTSD protein levels and activity in the mouse brain after stroke and neurons following OGD, with concurrent defects in lysosomal function.
